rounds.text: T & I Global Ltd offers an exceptionally compelling valuation setup, trading at a modest P/E of 12.5x and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.88x against a book value of 195 rupees, compared to sky-high sector benchmarks of 66.66x and 13.09x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This significant discount extends to its EV/EBITDA of 6.1x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 12.72x [E11]. Fundamental momentum is sharply inflecting in a positive direction, highlighted by a 50 percent surge in trailing twelve-month sales growth and a staggering 259 percent jump in compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. Operational quality is backed by pristine financial health, characterized by zero debt and an outstanding cash conversion rate of 2.71x where profits are fully backed by 19 crores in operating cash flow and 18 crores in free cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35, E36, E38]. Furthermore, efficiency has notably improved as the company's working capital requirements dramatically reduced from 57.7 days to 14.1 days [E60]. Conceded: [E16], [E19], [E20], [E43], [E63].

T & I Global Ltd carries fundamental structural weaknesses and an unfavorable valuation that the evidence soundly supports, starting with a rules-based screen score of just 38 out of 100 which generates a SELL rating with medium confidence [E65]. Long-term top-line growth is exceptionally sluggish, demonstrated by a compounded sales growth of just 2% over 10 years, 4% over 5 years, and a contraction of -6% over 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are equally underwhelming, highlighted by a stagnant 3-year median return on equity of 7% and a 5-year median ROE of only 9% [E27, E28]. Furthermore, valuation is already stretched against intrinsic value calculations, with a discounted cash flow model placing intrinsic value at Rs 152 per share against a higher market price of Rs 172, translating into a negative margin of safety of -13.2% [E43, E44]. Market participation also reflects distinct weakness, as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a poor relative-strength rating of 28 against the Nifty 500 [E48, E49]. Compounded further by severe historical volatility of 78.8% and a maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of -86.2%, the asset carries massive downside risks [E51, E52]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and generated strong operating and free cash flows of Rs 19 Cr and Rs 18 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E36, E38].

The bull's heavy reliance on low valuation multiples ignores that a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 152 sits below the current market price of Rs 172, creating a negative margin of safety of -13.2% [E43, E44]. While the bull highlights trailing spikes like 50% sales growth and 259% profit growth [E17, E21], it glosses over a multi-year decay featuring a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -6% and a 5-year profit contraction of -7% [E16, E19]. The touted P/E and P/B discounts relative to sector benchmarks [E6, E7] are offset by inferior returns on capital, as shown by a sub-par ROCE of 9.62% against the sector's 12.39% [E10] and a low median ROE of just 7% over the last year [E29]. Furthermore, earnings quality is inflated by Rs 5.43 Cr of other income [E64], and despite reporting profits, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield [E4, E61]. Conceded: [E1], [E2], [E11], [E35], [E36], [E38], [E60].
